question: According to recent reports, almost 42 %1 of honey imported into Belgium in 2024 originated from China. During the first nine months of 2025, the average import value of Chinese honey entering the EU was just EUR 1.20 per kilogram, compared with estimated European production costs of EUR 5.40 per kilogram.

Furthermore, the EU-coordinated investigation called From the Hives found that 46 % of the 320 imported honey samples examined were suspected of non-compliance with EU rules. Among samples originating from China, this figure reached 74 %, raising serious concerns about honey adulteration, consumer protection and unfair competition for EU beekeepers2. 1.

Can the Commission provide figures on the number of inspections carried out on honey imported into the EU from China in 2024, 2025 and 2026, including on the proportion of consignments found to be non-compliant?
What additional measures does the Commission intend to take to prevent adulterated honey from entering the EU market and to ensure effective enforcement of EU quality and traceability requirements?

Has the Commission assessed the impact of low-priced Chinese honey imports on the competitiveness of EU beekeepers, and does it envisage further measures to protect European producers against unfair competition?
